### Interpretation

**Headline.** On Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, none of the three base-model estimators of the behavior vector v_b clears the pre-registered validity bar on any of the six stored adapter families — 0/18 family×estimator verdicts VALID at the registered read-out (layer 14, mean-over-response, variant-matched base; 10 INVALID, 8 INDETERMINATE, N=31 run-cells). The best family-level median cosine anywhere is 0.27 against a 0.3 bar and a 0.73–0.99 seed-to-seed ceiling. P8's gating conclusion follows: **formula predictions driven by an estimated v_b are unidentified at the registered construction; downstream formula tests must use measured post-training writes.** One exploratory but seed-confirmed exception points at the read-out, not the estimator ladder: at layer 27, replaying the training data (E1) recovers the realized direction on both misalignment families (EM-turner cos 0.824 median across 3 seeds, selected on seed 42 at 0.827 and confirmed at 0.819/0.824 on seeds 137/256; EM-518 median 0.801 across 6 single-seed sources), while the prompting estimators (E2/E3) swing systematically NEGATIVE there (−0.56 to −0.84).

### Interpretation

**Headline.** On Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, none of the three base-model estimators of the behavior vector v_b validates on any of the six stored adapter families at the pre-registered read-out (layer 14, mean-over-response, variant-matched base): 0/18 family×estimator verdicts VALID, split 10 INVALID / 8 INDETERMINATE (N=31 run-cells). The best family-level median cosine anywhere is 0.274 against a 0.3 bar and a 0.72–0.99 seed-to-seed ceiling. The bridge to the P8 gate: the gate asks whether an *estimated* v_b can stand in for the measured post-training write in formula predictions, and an estimator that cannot be certified — whether INVALID (inside the null or reliably negative) or INDETERMINATE (above null, below the bar, or single-seed) — cannot, even though INDETERMINATE is not evidence of absence. So the gating conclusion: **formula predictions driven by an estimated v_b are unidentified at the registered construction; downstream formula tests should use measured post-training writes, unless the registered L27 E1 re-read (follow-up 1, free analysis) validates the late-layer estimator.** One exploratory exception points at the read-out, not the estimator ladder: at layer 27, replaying the training data (E1) recovers the realized direction on both misalignment families. On EM-turner the selected cell reads 0.827 on seed 42 with 0.819/0.824 on seeds 137/256 — but that "confirmation" is close to geometrically forced, because EM-turner's E1 is ONE shared estimator vector scored against three realized writes that are themselves 0.97-collinear, so the three values are not independent reads. The genuinely independent corroboration is EM-518: six different sources with six different training mixes under a different recipe (contrastive EM vs bad-medical SFT), single-seed each, w_shared median 0.801 at L27 (w_src median 0.765, range 0.755–0.844). Both reads carry the same unexcluded alternative: E1 teacher-forces literal training-mix rows, so late-layer agreement could partly reflect shared surface-token statistics rather than a recovered behavior state — the EM-518 corroboration addresses selection noise, not that confound.

| Family | E1 replay | E2 in-context | E3 describe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marker glyph (519) | INDETERMINATE (0.046) | INVALID (−0.014) | INDETERMINATE (0.033) |
| Bad-medical-advice EM (turner) | INVALID (0.022) | INVALID (−0.042) | INVALID (−0.167; w_shared −0.261) |

Two regimes hide inside INVALID: (a) cells indistinguishable from the random-direction null given the variance (e.g. EM-turner E1 at L14, |cos| ≤ 0.02), and (b) cells with *anti-alignment well outside the null* — E3 on EM-turner reads w_shared −0.221/−0.261/−0.263 on the three seed cells, ~7× the null's p99. On the replication structure of that anti-alignment, honestly: those three values are ONE estimator vector (E3 split-half reliability 0.55 on this family) scored against three 0.97-collinear targets, so they are one read, not three. What supports "reliably negative" is the magnitude plus the fact that the sign and size hold under the alternative target operationalization (same-variant scoring, 42/137/256 order: −0.289/−0.321/−0.320; see the sensitivity paragraph). The INDETERMINATE class (above the 0.027 null p95, below 0.3) is a named band, not a euphemism for zero: E1 on refusal-518 (0.193) and EM-518 (0.199) carries real but sub-bar signal, single-seed.

The two unreliable-E1 exceptions are informative: the marker family's per-seed E1 exclude-marker reads have split-half reliability ≈ 0 (0.071/0.049/−0.049, n=100 rows each) — once the marker token is excluded, the marker training data contains essentially no stable contrast signal for E1 to read; the behavior's entire training-data signature is the token itself. And the loc-474 context units sit at 0.54–0.69, intermediate. (The include-marker reads were stored and are barely different at L14: per-seed 0.040–0.069 vs 0.015–0.052 exclude — no token-identity artifact in either direction; include-marker rows are excluded from all aggregates by design.)

**H1 (fidelity ladder E1 > E2 > E3): not confirmed; not formally falsified.** 13/31 cells have no estimator above the null ("no ordering signal" — excluded from the ladder denominator as registered). On the 18 eligible cells the strict ordering holds on 2 (11%, vs the 60% confirmation bar); E3 ≥ E1 on 3/18 (not the majority the falsification clause requires). The three registered E3-over-E1 cells all sit on the marker-localized arm (loc-474 B1/C1/D1 on the shared-direction target; by best-target all four loc-474 contexts qualify, plus one fact cell) — the ladder violations concentrate exactly on the family where E1 is INVALID while the prompting estimators are INDETERMINATE. There is no fidelity ladder at L14 because there is almost no fidelity to order.

**H2 (EM most estimable): not confirmed at the registered read-out — but right about the family, wrong about the layer.** EM-turner has the most stable realized write (cross-seed ceiling 0.968–0.975) yet all three estimators are INVALID on it at L14. The exploratory grid reverses this at depth: E1 at L27 reaches 0.824 on EM-turner (one shared estimator vector; per-seed spread constrained by target collinearity, as above) and 0.801 median on EM-518 (six single-seed sources, cross-recipe) — the largest exploratory signal in the sweep, ~30× the null p95.

![Per-layer agreement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/1b765da63dd69d13e4a70c8d14506ffa04d5856f/figures/issue_602/exp_per_layer_agreement.png)

The prompting estimators collapse to anti-alignment at L27 on five of six families: E2 medians −0.56 to −0.82 (all but marker), E3 medians −0.20 to −0.84 on the same five (weakest on contrastive EM at −0.20, strongest on EM-turner at −0.84). The marker family is the systematic exception, and it completes a double dissociation worth its own sentence: at L27 the prompting estimators cross the 0.3 bar on marker — E2 w_src 0.47–0.55 at K=4 (0.48–0.57 at K=8) and E3 0.42–0.50, consistent across all three seed cells — exactly where marker E1 stays at floor (−0.04 median, exclude-marker) and where loc-474 E1 goes reliably negative (−0.24 median w_shared). The same collinearity caveat applies (one estimator vector per family against 0.96–0.99-collinear seed targets), and the alternative explanation for late-layer E1-on-EM stands: near the unembedding the realized shift is increasingly output-token-driven, and E1 teacher-forces the literal training completions, so late-layer agreement could partly reflect shared surface-token statistics. ### Human TL;DR (first pass)

**Headline.** I tried three ways of guessing, from the base model alone, which direction training will push the model for a behavior — replaying the training data, showing examples in context, and just describing the behavior — and at the read-out depth I registered, none of them is valid for any of the six behaviors I have trained adapters for.

**Takeaways.**
- The guesses aren't noisy — they're stable directions that simply point somewhere else. Some are even reliably anti-aligned with what training actually does.
- One real lead survives: much deeper in the network, replaying the training data does recover the training direction for both misalignment behaviors (two different recipes agree, ~0.8 cosine). Could still partly be a token-statistics artifact; cheap follow-up queued.
- One twist: at that same deep layer, prompting recovers the *marker* direction while replay fails on it — the exact mirror image. So "where you read" matters as much as "how you estimate".
- Practical upshot for the leakage formula: don't trust formula predictions built on estimated behavior vectors at mid-stack; use measured post-training writes until the deep-layer re-read is checked.

**How this updates me.** I now think the cheap "estimate the behavior vector from the base model" shortcut doesn't work at the layer everything else in the project reads from, and any formula result built on it would have been unidentified. What would change my mind: the free layer-27 re-read validating E1 against the behavioral panels — then the story becomes "right idea, wrong layer" instead of "estimators invalid".
